title: 1910.147 the control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) checklist
subtitle: Use while observing a servicing job under lockout or tagout and when reviewing the program records.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
Record each Defect with the corrective action and who owns it; do not let servicing continue while a Defect leaves anyone exposed.
The equipment manufacturer's instructions and your site rules may add checks.

sections.title: Program and written procedures
items: A program combining procedures, training and periodic inspections is in place and covers this equipment.
A documented procedure exists for this machine, or every one of the eight exception conditions applies to it.
The procedure lists specific steps to shut down, isolate, block and secure this machine.
The procedure states how locks or tags are placed, removed and transferred and who is responsible.
The procedure states how to test the machine to confirm the energy controls work.
Lockable isolators are locked, or the employer can show tagout gives full employee protection under (c)(3).
Isolators on equipment installed, replaced, majorly repaired, renovated or modified after January 2, 1990 accept a lockout device.

sections.title: Locks, tags and tag placement
items: Locks, tags, chains, wedges, key blocks, adapter pins or self-locking fasteners needed for the job are provided by the employer.
Energy control locks and tags are singularly identified and not used for anything else.
Devices match the facility standard for color, shape or size; tag print and format match too.
Every lock and tag shows the identity of the person who put it on.
Tags carry a warning such as Do Not Start, Do Not Energize or Do Not Operate.
Tags are fixed with a non-reusable, self-locking, hand-attachable tie with an unlocking strength of no less than 50 pounds.
Locks and tags are intact and suited to the environment they are left in for the job.
Tags in outdoor, wet or damp locations are intact with a legible message.
A tag on a lockable isolator is fastened at the point where the lock would go.
A tag that cannot be fixed to the isolating device is as close as safely possible to it, where anyone trying to operate the device would see it immediately.

sections.title: Applying controls on the job
items: Locks or tags are applied by the authorized employees doing the servicing.
Affected employees were told before controls were applied.
The authorized employee can state the energy types and magnitudes, their hazards and how to control them.
The machine was shut down using its established procedure, in an orderly way that added no hazard from the stoppage.
Every isolating device needed for this machine has been located and operated.
A lock or tag is on every isolating device.
Each lock holds its isolating device in the safe or off position.
Residual energy in springs, pressure systems, raised parts and similar sources has been relieved, restrained or made safe.
Where stored energy could reaccumulate to a hazardous level, isolation is re-verified until the work is complete or that possibility no longer exists.
The authorized employee verified isolation and deenergization before starting work.

sections.title: Release, testing, group work and handover
items: Nonessential items are gone and machine components are operationally intact before devices come off.
All employees are safely positioned or out of the area.
Affected employees are told the devices are off before the machine starts.
Each device is taken off by whoever put it on, or under the employer's documented removal procedure when that person is not at the facility.
When devices come off to test or position, the (f)(1) sequence is followed and controls go back on before servicing resumes.
On crew jobs, each authorized employee has a personal lock or tag on the group device or lockbox.
Protection is transferred in an orderly way between off-going and oncoming employees.
Where outside servicing personnel are on site, both employers have exchanged their procedures.

sections.title: Inspection and training records
items: An inspection of this procedure was done within the last year.
The inspector was an authorized employee not using the procedure being inspected.
The certification names the machine, date, employees included and inspector.
Authorized employees were trained in hazardous energy recognition, energy type and magnitude, and isolation methods.
Affected employees were instructed in the purpose and use of the procedure.
Where tags are used, training covered the limitations listed in (c)(7)(ii).
Retraining was given after any job assignment change, a machine or process change presenting a new hazard, or a procedure change.
Training records show each employee's name and training dates and are current.

references: 29 CFR 1910.147: The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, Part 1910 Subpart J (text as of 2026-11-09)
